notes.agrum: Reads the network's UAI file and its observations, the file Merlin reads.
notes.genfer: Genfer answers its own program: the Dice programs of its comparison in exact rationals, the population model in floating point (its masses summed over the bits of the circuit).
notes.geni: Geni computes in single precision and prints seven decimals, so differences of up to 5e-8 from the reference are its print precision.
notes.libdai: Reads the network's UAI file and its observations, the file Merlin reads.
notes.pgmpy: Reads the network's UAI file and its observations, the file Merlin reads.
notes.pluck: The time is the whole process's, with Julia loading Pluck; the in-process time leaves it out.
notes.prism: On the weather factory the model is Rubicon's PRISM model, not the program: the same Markov chain. On the other programs it is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value. The time includes the JVM's start.
notes.psi: Psi answers the Dice programs exactly, one run per component of the program's value, the times added. On its own linear regression it answers the posterior means of the continuous model, E(a) and E(b), which the circuit's bit queries do not have, so there is nothing to compare them with.
notes.sppl: SPPL answers the continuous model, with normal emissions as densities; the circuit rounds them to a grid, so the differences from the reference are that discretization.
notes.storm: On the weather factory the model is Rubicon's PRISM model, not the program: the same Markov chain. On the other programs it is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value.
notes.tensorinference: Reads the network's UAI file and its observations, the file Merlin reads; its time includes Julia's compilation and the search for a contraction order.

notes.sppl: SPPL answers the continuous model, with normal emissions as densities; the circuit rounds them to a grid, so the differences from the reference are that discretization.

# Conjugate Gaussians with low-probability observations (bit-blasting
# paper, Garg, Holtzen, Van den Broeck, Millstein, PLDI 2024, Section 2.3,
# Figures 5 and 6): a standard normal mean and two observations, 8 and 9,
# each normal around it with variance 1; the posterior is normal with mean
# 17/3 and variance 1/3. The paper plots it at 16 bits after the binary
# point and 2048 pieces; here the program is queried for its expectation.
# From Tractables/Alea.jl hybrid/benchmarks/conjugate_gaussians/
# conjugate_gaussians.jl at cf5e5b8 (Apache License 2.0): the bits and
# pieces, read from the command line there, are constants, and the
# plotting and results file are dropped; the body is otherwise unchanged.
using Alea, Distributions

const QUERY = :expectation
const bits = 16
const pieces = 2048
const DFiP = DistFix{8 + bits, bits}
const data = DFiP.([8.0, 9.0])
const add_arg = true

model() = @alea begin
    a = bitblast(DFiP, Normal(0, 1), pieces, -16.0, 16.0)
    for datapt in data
        gaussian_observe(DFiP, pieces, -16.0, 16.0, a, 1.0, datapt, add=add_arg, exp=false)
    end
    a
end
